s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of abnormal posturing and movement disorder following medication change
salient_findings: Bouts of extremely stiff, nonpainful neck that tilted her head involuntarily leftwards, upwards, and backwards in hyperextension
Conjugate deviation of the eyes upward or laterally
Involuntary posturing with head, neck, and spine arched backward
key_facts: 19-year-old female student
Admitted with grade III dyspnea
Prescribed diuretics and aspirin post-surgery
Started a new medication at low dose (25 mg per day) for two days
Dose was increased to 25 mg twice daily on the third day
Readmitted on the same evening after discharge on the fifth postoperative day
Subpulmonic ventricular septal defect
Severe aortic regurgitation due to right coronary cusp prolapse
Dilated left ventricle with ejection fraction of 40%
Mild aortic regurgitation on post-repair transesophageal echocardiographic assessment
Blood chemistry and electrolyte levels were within normal limits

shortlist.label: Acute Dystonic Reaction
shortlist.why_kept: Sudden onset of dystonic symptoms after medication change

shortlist.label: Tardive Dyskinesia
shortlist.why_kept: Involuntary movements and posturing following medication use

shortlist.label: Idiopathic Torsional Dystonia
shortlist.why_kept: Abnormal posturing and movement disorder without clear cause

shortlist.label: Antipsychotic-Induced Dystonia
shortlist.why_kept: Dystonic symptoms potentially related to medication side effects

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of an extremely stiff, nonpainful neck, conjugate deviation of the eyes, and involuntary posturing with head, neck, and spine arched backward, which started after increasing the dose of a new medication, are consistent with an acute dystonic reaction, a known side effect of certain medications.

rejected.label: Tardive Dyskinesia
rejected.why: Typically occurs after long-term use of antipsychotic medications, which is not indicated in this case

rejected.label: Drug-Induced Parkinsonism
rejected.why: Characterized by symptoms such as tremors, rigidity, and bradykinesia, which are not mentioned in the vignette

rejected.label: Idiopathic Torsional Dystonia
rejected.why: A chronic condition with a gradual onset, which does not fit the acute presentation in this case

rejected.label: Antipsychotic-Induced Dystonia
rejected.why: The vignette does not mention the use of antipsychotic medications

gold: Drug-induced acute dystonia caused by sacubitril/valsartan combination therapy
